chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, who said: Muhammad ibn Sama'at narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Abi Basir al-Muradi, from Abi Abdillah (Muhammad) Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about phlebotomy (cupping) and vomiting, and every flowing blood, so he said: There is no ablution required for it; rather, the ablution is only for what exits from your two sides, by which God has blessed you.
The compiler of this book - may God increase his honor - said: This means from urine or feces or wind (flatulence) or semen.

key_terms.حِجَامَة: Phlebotomy or cupping, a therapeutic procedure involving bloodletting.
key_terms.طَرَفَيْكَ: The two sides, referring to the urinary and anal passages.
key_terms.وُضُوء: Ritual ablution, a minor purification required before prayer.

ai.seo_question: Does bleeding from cupping or vomiting break ritual ablution (wudu) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the specific anatomical origin of impurities that nullify ablution, distinguishing general bodily discharges like blood or vomit from the 'two sides' (urinary and anal passages). This ruling reinforces the principle that wudu is only invalidated by excretions from these specific orifices, a foundational concept in Shia fiqh for determining ritual purity. The text explicitly links the 'two sides' to the Quranic description of human creation, grounding the legal ruling in scriptural evidence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-4 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sama’at, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Miskan, on the authority of Abi Basir al-Moradi: “I asked Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) regarding having phlebotomy performed and any blood that flows out of the body. The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘There is no need to make any ablutions since one must only make ablutions due to what leaves from the two sides by (the mechanisms bestowed to us due to) God’s Blessing.’”
The compiler of the book - may God increase his honor - said, “This means defecation, farting, urination, and ejaculation.”
